item_arguments_and_dependencies.title: The Heisenberg group of a finite-dimensional symplectic vector space
item_arguments_and_dependencies.statement:
Let $(V,\omega)$ be a finite-dimensional real symplectic vector space, so $V$
is a finite-dimensional real vector space and $\omega:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ is
an alternating, nondegenerate bilinear form
([[def-symplectic-vector-space]]). Define
$$H(V,\omega):=V\times\mathbb R$$with the product topology and multiplication$$
(v,t)(w,s)=\left(v+w,\ t+s-\frac12\omega(v,w)\right).
$$
The proposed identity is $(0,0)$, and the central coordinate is the subgroup
$j(\mathbb R)=\{(0,t):t\in\mathbb R\}$. The lemma
[[lem-heisenberg-group-lagrangian-splitting-and-dual-orbit]] verifies that this
is a second-countable locally compact topological group and that $j(\mathbb R)$
is its center.

The maps $j(t)=(0,t)$ and $\operatorname{pr}_V(v,t)=v$ form the central
extension shown below. The diagram records the maps; exactness is established
by the explicit kernel computation in the cited lemma.

```tikzcd
1 \arrow[r] & \mathbb R \arrow[r, hook, "j"] & H(V,\omega) \arrow[r, two heads, "\operatorname{pr}_V"] & V \arrow[r] & 1
```

item_arguments_and_dependencies.title: Incomplete tensor product of one-mode Hilbert spaces with a reference vector
item_arguments_and_dependencies.statement: For a unit reference vector Ω in L²(R), the coherent isometric embeddings L²(Rⁿ)→L²(Rᵐ), f↦f⊗Ω^{⊗(m−n)}, define an incomplete tensor product by Hilbert completion; each one-coordinate rank-one projection P_j^Φ for a unit Φ is well-defined and orthogonal.
item_arguments_and_dependencies.proof_strategy: Verify the embeddings are coherent isometries by Fubini, define the compatible union, then show the coordinate projection formulas are contractions compatible with the embeddings.

item_arguments_and_dependencies.title: The universal Weyl C*-algebra
item_arguments_and_dependencies.statement:
Let $(V,\omega)$ be a finite-dimensional real symplectic vector space and let
$\lambda\in\mathbb R$. Regard the additive group underlying $V$ as discrete
for this construction, and define
$$m_\lambda(v,w):=e^{-i\lambda\omega(v,w)/2}.$$
Let $A_0(V,\omega,\lambda)=\mathbb C^{(V)}$ be the complex vector space of
finitely supported functions on $V$, with basis $(\delta_v)_{v\in V}$ and
unit $\delta_0$. Define
$$\delta_v\delta_w=m_\lambda(v,w)\delta_{v+w},\qquad \delta_v^*=\delta_{-v},$$
and extend multiplication bilinearly and the involution conjugate-linearly.
Here a linear functional $\varphi:A_0\to\mathbb C$ is **positive unital** if
$\varphi(a^*a)\ge0$ for every $a\in A_0$ and $\varphi(\delta_0)=1$. Put
$N_\varphi=\{a\in A_0:\varphi(a^*a)=0\}$, equip $A_0/N_\varphi$ with
$$\langle[a],[b]\rangle_\varphi:=\varphi(b^*a),$$
and let $\pi_\varphi$ be left multiplication on the Hilbert completion of
this quotient. The lemma
[[lem-universal-weyl-c-star-algebra-is-well-defined]] verifies that these
quotients and representations are well-defined.
Define the universal C*-seminorm and completion by
$$\|a\|_u:=\sup_{\varphi}\|\pi_\varphi(a)\|,\qquad C^*_{\mathrm W}(V,\omega,\lambda):=\overline{A_0/\ker\|\cdot\|_u}^{\,\|\cdot\|_u}.$$
The lemma [[lem-universal-weyl-c-star-algebra-is-well-defined]] proves that
the twisted algebra and GNS representations are well-defined, the seminorm is
finite and nonzero, and the completion is universal for unitary generators
with the displayed Weyl relations. Countable Choice is included through the
Hilbert completions in that construction.

item_arguments_and_dependencies.title: Regular Weyl systems and irreducibility
item_arguments_and_dependencies.statement:
Fix a finite-dimensional real symplectic vector space $(V,\omega)$ and a real
parameter $\lambda$. A **Weyl system with parameter $\lambda$** on a nonzero
complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ is a map $W:V\to U(\mathcal H)$ such that
$$W(0)=I,\qquad W(v)W(w)=e^{-i\lambda\omega(v,w)/2}W(v+w)\quad(v,w\in V).$$
It is **regular** when, for every $v\in V$, the map
$t\mapsto W(tv)$ is strongly continuous on $\mathbb R$. It is
**irreducible** when the only closed subspaces invariant under every $W(v)$ are
$\{0\}$ and $\mathcal H$, as in
[[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]].

Each $W(v)$ is unitary. Substituting $w=-v$ in the relation gives
$W(v)W(-v)=I$, because $\omega(v,-v)=0$; hence
$W(v)^*=W(-v)$. The scalar $\lambda$ is the central character parameter:
the associated representation of [[def-heisenberg-group-of-a-symplectic-vector-space]]
acts on $(0,t)$ by $e^{i\lambda t}I$.

item_arguments_and_dependencies.title: Heisenberg group polarization and the fixed-central-character orbit
item_arguments_and_dependencies.statement: In symplectic coordinates the Heisenberg group is a topological semidirect product of an abelian normal subgroup N=R^n×R by a Lagrangian R^n; for every nonzero central parameter λ, the corresponding K-action on the characters of N with central character t↦e^{iλt} is free and transitive.
item_arguments_and_dependencies.proof_strategy: Verify the cocycle and semidirect multiplication directly, then compute the dual action on coordinate characters.

item_arguments_and_dependencies.title: The universal Weyl norm is finite and has the C*-completion property
item_arguments_and_dependencies.statement: The symplectic phase is a normalized 2-cocycle, the twisted finite-support algebra has the stated involution, and its supremum over cyclic *-representations is a finite nonzero C*-seminorm whose quotient completion is universal for unitary Weyl generators.
item_arguments_and_dependencies.proof_strategy: Prove the cocycle identity, construct algebraic GNS representations of positive states, bound every representation by the ℓ¹ coefficient norm, and complete the quotient.

item_arguments_and_dependencies.title: The Schrödinger Weyl system is regular and irreducible
item_arguments_and_dependencies.statement: For n≥0 and λ≠0, the operators on L²(R^n), (Sλ(q,p,z)f)(x)=e^{iλz+iλp·(x−q/2)}f(x−q), form a strongly continuous irreducible unitary representation of the stated Heisenberg group; its Weyl operators satisfy the fixed phase convention.
item_arguments_and_dependencies.proof_strategy: Check the multiplication law and strong continuity directly; prove irreducibility by Fourier uniqueness and Tonelli’s theorem.
item_arguments_and_dependencies.axioms: Countable Choice is used only through L² translation continuity and L¹ Fourier inversion; the phase calculation and Tonelli contradiction are choice-free.

item_arguments_and_dependencies.title: The Gaussian Weyl average is a rank-one projection
item_arguments_and_dependencies.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. In the one-mode Schrödinger Weyl system
$W(q,p)f(x)=e^{i(p x-pq/2)}f(x-q)$ on $L^2(\mathbb R)$, for $a>0$ put
$\Omega_a(x)=(a/\pi)^{1/4}e^{-ax^2/2}$. The weak Weyl average

$$A_a:=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^2}e^{-aq^2/4-p^2/(4a)}W(q,p)\,dq\,dp$$
is the orthogonal projection $f\mapsto\langle f,\Omega_a\rangle\Omega_a$, and $\operatorname{span}\{W(q,p)\Omega_a:q,p\in\mathbb R\}$ is dense in $L^2(\mathbb R)$. If a bounded operator intertwines two regular one-mode Weyl systems with this phase, their averages exist and it intertwines them. In an incomplete tensor product of copies of this representation, $A_a$ acts on one coordinate as the rank-one projection onto $\Omega_a$ tensored with the identity on all other coordinates.
item_arguments_and_dependencies.proof_strategy: Compute the integral kernel by the Gaussian Fourier transform, then use Fourier uniqueness to prove totality.
item_arguments_and_dependencies.axioms: Countable Choice is inherited from the L² Hilbert structures, L² density, and L¹ Fourier inversion. The Gaussian integral identity and operator intertwinement are choice-free.

item_arguments_and_dependencies.title: Stone–von Neumann uniqueness for finite-dimensional regular Weyl systems
item_arguments_and_dependencies.statement: Assume AC. For a finite-dimensional real symplectic space (V,ω) and real λ≠0, every nonzero irreducible regular Weyl system with W(v)W(w)=e^(−iλω(v,w)/2)W(v+w) is unitarily equivalent to the Schrödinger system on L²(R^n); the latter is irreducible, so the equivalence class exists and is unique.
item_arguments_and_dependencies.proof_strategy: Convert the Weyl system to a Heisenberg-group representation, use the spectral measure of its abelian normal subgroup to obtain a transitive system on the fixed-central-character orbit, and apply Mackey imprimitivity with trivial stabilizer.
item_arguments_and_dependencies.axioms: AC is required by the published spectral-measure, transitive-system, and Mackey-imprimitivity suppliers. The countable dense sets and conull intersections below are explicitly indexed by rational coordinates and a fixed countable dense subset, so they require no additional choice. The separately cited Schrödinger-model lemma has its own Countable Choice dependency.

item_arguments_and_dependencies.title: The universal Weyl C*-algebra has nonregular representations
item_arguments_and_dependencies.statement:
Let $V=\mathbb R^2$ with its standard symplectic form and fix
$\lambda\ne0$. The universal Weyl $C^*$-algebra
$C^*_{\mathrm W}(V,\omega,\lambda)$ has a representation in which the Weyl
generators are not strongly continuous on real lines. Thus its universal
property does not restrict representations to the regular ones.
item_arguments_and_dependencies.axioms: Countable Choice is inherited through the stated Hilbert-space and universal-completion constructions; the discontinuity calculation is choice-free.

item_arguments_and_dependencies.statement: On the standard symplectic plane at λ=0, every real-linear character defines a regular irreducible one-dimensional Weyl system; the characters ℓ₀(q,p)=0 and ℓ₁(q,p)=πq are inequivalent.

item_arguments_and_dependencies.title: The one-mode Schrödinger formulas and their phase
item_arguments_and_dependencies.statement:
Let $\lambda\ne0$. On $L^2(\mathbb R)$ define
$U_qf(x)=f(x-q)$ and $V_pf(x)=e^{i\lambda px}f(x)$. Then
$U_qV_p=e^{-i\lambda qp}V_pU_q$. The phase-corrected operators
$$W_\lambda(q,p):=e^{i\lambda qp/2}U_qV_p$$
satisfy $W_\lambda(q,p)W_\lambda(q',p')=
e^{-i\lambda(qp'-pq')/2}W_\lambda(q+q',p+p')$ and are exactly the
one-mode Schrödinger Weyl operators in
[[lem-schrodinger-weyl-system-is-regular-and-irreducible]].

item_arguments_and_dependencies.title: Infinitely many modes admit inequivalent irreducible regular Weyl representations
item_arguments_and_dependencies.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice.

Let $V=c_{00}(\mathbb N;\mathbb R^2)$ be the real vector space of finitely
supported sequences $v=((q_j,p_j))_{j\ge1}$, with
$\omega(v,w)=\sum_j(q_jp'_j-p_jq'_j)$; this finite sum defines a nondegenerate
alternating form. For $a=1,2$, let $\mathcal H_a$ be the incomplete tensor
product of copies of $L^2(\mathbb R)$ with reference vector
$\Omega_a(x)=(a/\pi)^{1/4}e^{-ax^2/2}$. The finite-support operators

$$\mathcal W_a(v)=\bigotimes_{j\ge1}W_1(q_j,p_j),\qquad (W_1(q,p)f)(x)=e^{ip(x-q/2)}f(x-q),$$
where all but finitely many factors are the identity, define irreducible Weyl representations with phase $e^{-i\omega(v,w)/2}$ that are strongly continuous on every real line. They are inequivalent: a common local Gaussian average has expectation $1$ in the first reference vector and limiting expectation $2\sqrt2/3<1$ in every unit vector of the second representation.
item_arguments_and_dependencies.axioms: Countable Choice is used for the L² Hilbert structures and Hilbert completions, finite box-step density, and one-mode Gaussian/L² density; the finite-support formulas and overlap limit require no further choice.

transitive_interfaces_audited.hypotheses: AC; second-countable locally compact Hausdorff abelian N; strongly continuous unitary representation; separable Hilbert space; the theorem supplies a unique regular PVM and covariance.

AC; second-countable locally compact Hausdorff G; closed subgroup N; transitive system on G/N; separable Hilbert space; normalized full-support Radon measure; strongly continuous subgroup representation.
Separable measurable Hilbert fibers and equality of the multiplication operators/PVMs; field equality is used only almost everywhere and then extended by continuity on a common dense set.
The real-line character classification and the finite-product dual theorem are used; only the finite-product clause is invoked, which is choice-free.

Countable Choice is carried where required by translation continuity, Fourier inversion, product density and Hilbert completions; Tonelli/Fubini are applied to the stated nonnegative or absolutely integrable kernels.
